newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 3.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 3.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday:

* U.S. stocks and bonds rallied on Wednesday as the Federal Reserve kept interest rates steady, while the dollar surged to another 40-month peak against the German mark. The blue-chip Dow Jones industrial average ended up 73.05 points at 7,795.38, which was just below its June 20 record close of 7,796.51.

* Indonesia on Wednesday welcomed a fall in inflation during June, and said it expected the year-on-year rate to fall below six percent in calendar 1997. Figures released earlier showed that Indonesia's consumer price index (CPI) fell 0.17 percent month-to-month in June, after a rise of 0.19 percent in May.

* Jakarta stocks end slightly lower on Wednesday after hitting another record high for the third time this week as the market went through a consolidation phase, brokers said. The Jakarta Composite Index eased 1.46 points, or 0.20 percent, to 730.16 points after hitting a record high of 734.02 points early in the day.
* On Wednesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,432.50/34.50 at 0145 GMT, compared with an opening 2,433.00/2,433.50.
* Cigarette maker HM Sampoerna on market talk that the firm was likely to increase starting early next week.
* Blue chip telecommunication firm PT Telkom after president director Asman Akhir Nasution reportedly told parliament that the firm's total debt was about 4.8 trillion rupiah.
* Property firm Surya Semesta and chemical firm Eterindo Wahana on market talk of possible private placements.

* Small-sized poultry Cipendawa Farm Enterprises following reports that it would buy a 100 percent stake in PT Buana Superior Feedmeal for 40 billion rupiah. Also on recent reports of a proposed 80 billion rupiah rights issue.

* Cable maker Gajah Tunggal Kabel Indonesia on reports that it had signed a memorandum of understanding with PT Tranfindo Perkasa and PT Putera Sutraco Mulia to take over the stake of the two companies in PT Putera Ometraco Electric.

* Property firm Jakarta International Hotel Development after the Indonesiana Observer newspaper reported on Thursday that the firm will sell 600 billion rupiah of fixed-rated bonds with a coupon of 16 percent.
* Pharmaceutical firm Tempo Scan on a report in Bisnis Indonesia that a founding shareholder had sold 20 million shares, or a 13 percent stake, through a private placement.
* Property firm Bakrieland following reports that it will increase its authorised capital ahead of a planned rights issue this year. No details of the rights issue plan were available.
